blocks.task_summary: Show that L = (3/4)sec(alpha) + 6cosec(alpha) by expressing AC and CB using right-triangle trigonometry on the diagram.
method_path: Express AC via cos(alpha) = (3/4)/AC giving AC = (3/4)sec(alpha)
Express CB via sin(alpha) = 6/CB giving CB = 6cosec(alpha)
Sum AC + CB to obtain L = (3/4)sec(alpha) + 6cosec(alpha)

evidence.basis: A1 for AC = (3/4)sec(alpha); A1 for CB = 6cosec(alpha); concluding L = (3/4)sec(alpha) + 6cosec(alpha) AG.

blocks.task_summary: (i) Find dL/d(alpha). (ii) When dL/d(alpha) = 0, show that alpha = arctan 2.
method_path: Differentiate L: dL/d(alpha) = (3/4)sec(alpha)tan(alpha) - 6cosec(alpha)cot(alpha)
Rewrite derivative in terms of sin(alpha), cos(alpha) or tan(alpha)
Set dL/d(alpha) = 0 and simplify
Obtain tan^3(alpha) = 8
Take cube root: tan(alpha) = 2
Conclude alpha = arctan 2
accepted_alternatives: Derivative equivalently expressed as (3sin(alpha))/(4cos^2(alpha)) - (6cos(alpha))/sin^2(alpha) or via tan(alpha) factors.

evidence.basis: (b)(i) A1 for dL/d(alpha) = (3/4)sec(alpha)tan(alpha) - 6cosec(alpha)cot(alpha). (b)(ii) (M1) for writing derivative in terms of sin,cos or tan; (A1) for setting to zero and manipulating; A1 for tan^3(alpha)=8; A1 for tan(alpha)=2; A1 for alpha=arctan2 AG.

blocks.task_summary: (i) Find d^2L/d(alpha)^2. (ii) When alpha = arctan 2, show that d^2L/d(alpha)^2 = (45*sqrt(5))/4.
method_path: Apply product rule to dL/d(alpha) to find d^2L/d(alpha)^2
Obtain terms: (3/4)sec(alpha)tan^2(alpha)+(3/4)sec^3(alpha)+6cosec(alpha)cot^2(alpha)+6cosec^3(alpha)
Use right triangle for tan(alpha)=2 to find sec(alpha)=sqrt(5), cosec(alpha)=sqrt(5)/2, cot(alpha)=1/2
Substitute ratios into d^2L/d(alpha)^2
Simplify to (45*sqrt(5))/4
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent simplifications using trigonometric identities; ratios may be found via identities rather than right triangle.

evidence.basis: (c)(i) (M1) for product rule attempt; A1 for sec terms; A1 for cosec terms. (c)(ii) (M1) for finding trig ratios from tan(alpha)=2; (A1) for one correct ratio; A2 for correct substitution and simplification to (45*sqrt(5))/4 AG.

blocks.task_summary: (i) Justify that L is a minimum when alpha = arctan 2. (ii) Determine the minimum value of L.
method_path: Note d^2L/d(alpha)^2 > 0 at alpha = arctan 2, confirming concave up
Conclude L is a minimum since dL/d(alpha)=0 and d^2L/d(alpha)^2 > 0
Substitute sec(alpha)=sqrt(5), cosec(alpha)=sqrt(5)/2 into L
Simplify: L_min = (3/4)sqrt(5) + 6(sqrt(5)/2) = (15*sqrt(5))/4

evidence.basis: (d)(i) R1 for d^2L/d(alpha)^2 > 0 or concave up, when dL/d(alpha)=0 hence minimum. (d)(ii) (A1) for L_min = (3/4)sqrt(5) + 6(sqrt(5)/2); A1 for (15*sqrt(5))/4.

blocks.task_summary: Determine whether a pole of length 11.25 m can be carried horizontally from the passageway into the room, giving a reason.
method_path: Recognise L_min = (15*sqrt(5))/4 is the shortest AB touching corner C
Evaluate L_min approx 8.39 m
Compare pole length 11.25 m with L_min
Conclude pole cannot be carried since 11.25 > L_min

evidence.basis: R1 for comparative reasoning showing L_min < 11.25 (or equivalent); A1 for concluding the pole cannot be carried horizontally. Note: markscheme states Do not award R0A1.
